title: DAW integration: transport and tempo sync (Link)
description:
## Intent

As a performer, I want Apricity to follow the DAW's tempo and transport over Link, so that the web app or the Swift app becomes a synced sampler beside my set: a score edit re-renders and drops in on the next bar while the DAW keeps playing.

## Why it fits

The engine already renders ahead and swaps arrangements at the bar line with a crossfade, so it is built for a clock it does not own. The DAW leads; Apricity follows.

## Scope

- Link peer in the native engine (Rust binding); phase-aligned start at the next bar.
- Tempo changes re-warp the arrangement ahead of the beat.
- Browser: Link is not reachable from a page, so the local server hosts the peer and streams clock to the AudioWorklet.

## Not included

- Sending audio into the DAW (routing is the user's system audio / a loopback driver).

## Definition of done

- Two peers stay within one beat-phase tolerance over a 10-minute run (measured in a test harness).
- Stories for start-on-bar, tempo change, and stop.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
## Plan: transport and tempo over Link (Plan Link Sync)

### Epics, in delivery order
1. **M0: Spike** (apricitus-022988): binding and build targets, RT-safe capture, host-time mapping, varispeed bridge vs re-phase, browser clock accuracy, cloud reachability, macOS permission. Leaves `design/link.md`, no product code. 4 tasks.
2. **M1: The engine follows a beat clock** (apricitus-e661eb): `apricity-engine::clock`, the `Mixer` follows a clock line, bridge + drift trim, re-warp at the clock's tempo, wasm export. 4 stories, 5 tasks, 2 chores (plus the red-spec task).
3. **M2: `apricity play --link`** (apricitus-97a1dd): new native-only crate `apricity-link`, `play --link --quantum --no-start-stop --latency`, `apricity link`. 5 stories, 6 tasks, 2 chores.
4. **M3: The web app through `apricity serve --link`** (apricitus-75c473): `/link` WebSocket, `schema/link-clock.schema.json`, `web/src/audio/link-clock.ts`, player and worklet, UI needs for the web session. 3 stories, 6 tasks, 2 chores.
5. **M4: Proven in phase** (apricitus-4e9cee): 10-minute native and browser harnesses with reports, the DAW checklist, numbers posted here. 3 stories, 3 tasks, 1 chore.

### Key decisions (proposed; M0 confirms)
- **Apricity only follows.** It never commits a tempo or a start/stop to the session. It proposes the score's tempo only when it is alone at join time; later `tempo` edits are reported as not used while linked.
- **What Link doesn't share:** song position and time signature. Bar 1 lands on a session bar line; the quantum defaults to the score's time signature (`--quantum` overrides).
- **Start/stop sync on by default**; `--no-start-stop` for peers that don't share it.
- **Tempo changes:** a varispeed bridge keeps the beat until the arrangement re-warped at the new tempo lands on the next bar line; a re-render debounce for ramps; cached renders reused when a tempo comes back.
- **Crates:** the clock math in `apricity-engine` (it builds for wasm); the SDK only in the native `apricity-link`.
- **Browser:** the peer lives in the Rust `apricity serve`, not `server.py` (being retired), so there is no Python part. No language or manifest change; one new schema for the wire messages.
- **Words:** Link, Link session, peer, quantum, phase, start/stop sync. Not "sync" alone (`apricity sync` is the library) and not "follow" alone (`transpose follow`).
- **Tolerance proposal:** native 3 ms, browser 10 ms, at p99 and max.

### Open questions for the owner
1. Is the tolerance proposal right? The initiative says "one beat-phase tolerance"; the harness needs numbers.
2. Should start/stop sync be on by default?
3. Should the cloud app get Link through a local helper, or stay local-only (depends on M0's reachability finding)?
4. iOS / Swift app: the SDK's iOS terms differ from the desktop's (joins apricitus-874f56). Out of scope here, but it decides whether `apricity-link` is reusable there.
5. Should the 10-minute harnesses run in CI on a schedule?
6. May `apricity play --link` start a session at the score's tempo when alone (a DAW that joins later adopts it, if M0 confirms Link merges that way)?

### Dependencies
No hard dependency on the other DAW initiatives (apricitus-6edba8, apricitus-d7746d, apricitus-5562e0). Relates to apricitus-8edd5f, apricitus-205813, apricitus-874f56, apricitus-1f0e91, apricitus-92b5b5, apricitus-7edd75; the browser harness is blocked by apricitus-94da2e.

comments.text:
## Decisions on the open questions (2026-09-26, orchestrator, on the owner's behalf)

1. **Tolerances:** 3 ms native, 10 ms browser, measured as beat-phase error at 120 BPM over the 10-minute run. M0 may tighten them, never loosen without a comment here.
2. **Start/stop sync:** on by default; `--no-start-stop` opts out. A performer pressing play in the DAW expects Apricity to start.
3. **Cloud app:** local-only. `apricity serve --link` is the only browser path in this initiative; the cloud app gets no Link.
4. **iOS:** out of scope. Build `apricity-link` with no desktop assumptions so it can be reused, but plan no iOS work here; licensing stays with apricitus-874f56.
5. **CI:** the 10-minute harnesses do not run in CI (they need real network peers). CI runs a short deterministic test against a simulated clock; the harnesses are a script run before closing M4 and recorded in its log.
6. **Lone peer:** yes, `apricity play --link` starts a session at the score's tempo when alone, if M0 confirms a joining DAW adopts it.
